Pittsburgh made the call to bench Rodgers after offensive struggles led to consecutive losses following a 6-2 start

        Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy benched quarterback Aaron Rodgers, the quarterback he developed into a four-time NFL MVP and Super Bowl XLV MVP with the Green Bay Packers, on Tuesday night just shy of the future Hall of Famer's 43rd birthday. Seven-year NFL veteran Mason Rudolph will start in place of the inactive Rodgers for the Steelers on Friday against the AFC West-leading Denver Broncos (8-2).
Rodgers is being benched after the Steelers (6-4) lost consecutive games following their 6-2 start to the 2026 season. Pittsburgh was crushed 38-18 at the Cincinnati Bengals on "Sunday Night Football in Week 10 before losing 19-16 against the Philadelphia Eagles, a team that was on a seven-game losing streak, in Week 11.  In those two defeats, Rodgers averaged under 5.5 yards per pass attempt in consecutive games for just the second time in the past 10 seasons (Weeks 4-5 of the 2024 season). He has never had such a streak span three games. Rodgers being benched makes sense when watching the tape. He plays the quarterback position not to get hit anymore. He is just shy of his 43rd birthday on Dec. 2, so it makes sense that the 2026 season will be his last. Rodgers completed 30 of his 44 throws for 227 yards and a touchdown and was also the Steelers' leading rusher (29 yards on 5 carries) in the deflating 19-16 loss against the Eagles as Pittsburgh fell behind 13-0 after their first four drives ended in a turnover on downs and three punts, and Rodgers was never able to guide the Steelers out of that hole. He ranks 19th in the NFL in passer rating (86.6) and 28th in expected points added per dropback (-0.11) among 32 qualified quarterbacks this season. He is completing 60.9% for 2,241 yards passing with 16 passing touchdowns and 6 interceptions. Rodgers' average time to throw of 2.85 seconds stands as the sixth fastest in the entire NFL this season. His 543 career passing touchdowns are the third most in NFL history, and he is the league's all-time leader in touchdown-to-interception ratio (4.21, 543-129). His 6.2 yards per pass attempt (26th in the NFL this season) and 86.6 passer rating 19th in the NFL this season) are both the lowest of his 19 seasons as an NFL starting quarterback. Rodgers' 13.6% off target pass rate ranks as the eighth worst in the league this season, according to TruMedia. Aaron Rodgers all-time ranksNFL all-time rankQB wins1695thPass yards68,5155thPass TD5433rdTD-INT543-1291stPasser rating101.64thNFL MVPs42nd* Led Packers to win in Super Bowl XLV as Super Bowl XLV MVP (2010 season)
Rudolph will make his 20th career start in his 39th game played on Black Friday against the Broncos. He has a career 64.2% completion percentage with 4,927 yards passing, 30 touchdowns and 22 interceptions for an 84.3 passer rating. Six of his seven NFL seasons have been with the Steelers since Pittsburgh drafted him in the third round of the 2018 NFL Draft with the 76 overall pick. Rudolph is 9-9-1 in his career as an NFL starting quarterback with 30 passing touchdowns and 22 interceptions in his starts. His last start came in place of an injured Rodgers in Week 12 of the 2026 season at the Chicago Bears in a 31-28 defeat. Rudolph completed 24 of his 31 throws (77.4%) for 171 passing yards, a passing touchdown and an interception for an 86.9 passer rating.

In the end, Allen will make the big play late to win it. Pick: Bills 30, Chiefs 26Denver Broncos at Pittsburgh Steelers (+3)Friday, 3 p.m., streaming on Amazon PrimeThis Friday game pits two teams who would be in the playoffs right now. The Colts have packed it in, so the Giants take it. Pick: Giants 27, Colts 10New York Jets at Miami Dolphins (+3.5)Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+)The Jets are playing consecutive road games, while the Dolphins are home for the first time in three weeks. The Jets played well in beating the Chargers last week, while Miami lost to the Bills. The Dolphins are limited on offense, but the Jets' defense has struggled. Look for Miami to hang around. Pick: Jets 23, Dolphins 21Atlanta Falcons at Minnesota Vikings (-7)Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free)The Vikings are home after getting blown out by the 49ers in Mexico. The Falcons are off a bye. The Minnesota offense struggled against the 49ers, but the Falcons have had defensive problems lately. Look for the Minnesota defense to get back on track as well. Vikings take it. 
Pick: Vikings 28, Falcons 14Tennessee Titans at Jacksonville Jaguars (-14.5)Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free)The Jaguars are coming off a bad showing in the loss to the Giants, while Tennessee gave up 51 to the Cowboys last week. Ouch. The Jaguars scored 40 against them two weeks ago. They won't get that many here, but it will still be ugly as Trevor Lawrence and the passing game get back on track. Pick: Jaguars 33, Titans 13Baltimore Ravens at Houston Texans (-7)Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+)This is essentially a playoff game of sorts for these two. The loser is pretty much done. The Texans are home off a Thursday game, while the Ravens are playing consecutive road games. Edge Houston. The Texans have played well on offense, and the Ravens' defense is a mess. Look for a big day for C.J. Stroud. Pick: Texans 31, Ravens 23New England Patriots at Los Angeles Chargers (-1.5)Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+)This was once scheduled for prime time, but it was moved because both teams have flopped this year. The Patriots will start Tommy DeVito for the injured Drake Maye. That's a problem. The Chargers might not have Justin Herbert (concussion) either, which would put D.J. Uiagalelei in as the starter. He's thrown seven passes in his career. Even so, give me the home team here. 
Pick: Chargers 23, Patriots 16Washington Commanders (-7) at Arizona Cardinals Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free)The Commanders are coming off an impressive home victory Monday night over the Bengals, while the Cardinals got rocked by the Chiefs last week. Arizona has big-time issues and fired the defensive coordinator this week. That defense will struggle to stop Jayden Daniels. The Commanders stay hot. Pick: Commanders 30, Cardinals 19Seattle Seahawks at San Francisco 49ers (-3.5)Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free)The 49ers have the best record in the NFC and seem to be cruising to the division title. But Seattle can slow that talk down here with a victory. That will be tough to do on the road. Look for a lower-scoring game in the second division game between the two — the 49ers won the first — and San Francisco will win it late.Pick: 49ers 21, Seahawks 17Las Vegas Raiders at Cleveland Browns (-4.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free)This has been flexed to prime time because the Browns would be a playoff team right now. Plus, the Raiders have rookie Fernando Mendoza making his third start. The Raiders are playing consecutive road games, and Cleveland is off a bye. Big edge to the Browns as they win it behind their defense. 
Pick: Browns 27, Raiders 19Carolina Panthers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-3)Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free)The Panthers can take a stronghold on the division with a victory here.  They come in with defensive issues, but the Bucs have problems in the passing game. So what gives? I think the Tampa Bay defense will play well here and the Bucs will run it right at Carolina to win it like they did in the first meeting.Pick: Bucs 23, Panthers 17

Young has been a mess as a scorer this season, shooting just 36.4% from the floor and 32.5% on 3s

        The Washington Wizards entered Tuesday with a 7-11 record. In their seven wins, Trae Young is averaging just under 11.3 shot attempts per game. In those 11 losses, he's averaging 13.3. It's a small difference, but a notable one. The Wizards came into play Tuesday on a three-game winning streak, and a meaningful part of that streak has been Young spending less time on the ball. In Washington's first 15 games, he averaged around 6.6 minutes of possession per game, tied for the third-most in the league. He's down to 4.5 in his last three games. He's dribbling around one fewer time per touch, and his average possession per touch is down around a second. These aren't glaring changes, but they've been helpful ones. It's not a coincidence, for example, that No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa's two best offensive games have come in this stretch. Young, 28, has been a mess as a scorer this season. He's shooting just 36.4% from the floor and 32.5% on 3s. He's barely getting to the basket and struggling mightily when he's in the paint. He can't beat defenders nearly as easily off the dribble as he once could. Getting the ball out of his hands a bit more has been essential. 
It's been an intentional shift on Washington's part. Wizards officials have asked Young to focus less on his own scoring and instead emphasize his playmaking, according to The Athletic. Washington certainly won't complain about a 24-to-7 assist-to-turnover ratio in that stretch. Young, despite his noticeable decline as a scorer, remains a stellar passer. That's typically how star decline works. It comes in bits and pieces. Even as essential components of a player's game degrade, years of accumulated basketball IQ allow him to continue finding ways to contribute. After years of abject tanking, the Wizards seemingly wanted an offensive organizer around to help give their younger players some structure. Young can still do that.
But we're in an increasingly financially unforgiving NBA, and the Wizards aren't paying Young a contributor's salary. They're paying him star money, and they chose to do so after just five relatively quiet games with him a season ago. His four-year, $212 million max contract will pay him at the top of the market through the end of Dybantsa's rookie deal. With Anthony Davis on the books through the end of Kyshawn George and Alex Sarr's rookie deals, the Wizards effectively traded the roster-building flexibility those cheap rookie deals afforded them for two declining stars. Davis has justified the investment, at least as an asset. They haven't extended him. They could potentially flip him for more than they paid him. Young has not.And that's the dilemma the Wizards are now in. 
        
            
                NBA Hater Report: Celtics can't shoot, neither can Trae Young and James Harden isn't close to a top 10 player
                
                    Brad Botkin                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
A daunting shift for YoungClearly, less Young leads to more winning for the Wizards. But getting enough out of him to justify that enormous contract almost certainly requires more than they're currently getting. The entire value proposition of employing Young rests on him being a high-usage offensive engine. He just doesn't provide enough off-ball offensive value to justify what he gives up defensively at a max price point.
Take his shooting, for example. "Trae's got so much gravity," Wizards coach Brian Keefe told The Athletic. "When he plays off the ball, he's going to draw people, and then we're getting into actions with him on the second side that have been really good." There's something to this in theory, especially since gravity tends to rest more on reputation than reality. But Young has never been a consistently reliable catch-and-shoot player. He's averaging less than two catch-and-shoot 3-point attempts per game this season and has made around 28% of them. He's never averaged more than two catch-and-shoot 3-point attempts per game in a season. Maybe he improves if his role demands more of these shots, but this is his ninth NBA season. That sort of shift this late in a career is rare.It's a daunting change. Young spent most of his seven-and-a-half-year Atlanta Hawks run as almost entirely an on-ball player. He's never scored more than 39 points off of cuts in a single season. He has none this season. He's never been an especially active mover or screener, and even if he's grown on that front over the last few years, that's from a starting point of essentially zero. Asking Young to be less of a heliocentric shot creator is essentially asking Young to be a different player entirely.
That was the danger in paying Young sight unseen. They had no idea how he'd fit on this roster when they ponied up a max deal. If he'd picked up his player option and made this a prove-it season, they could have worked out the kinks and tried to sign him to a more appropriate deal next summer. The obvious argument here is that Young might have left had the Wizards refused to give him a long-term extension, but the counter here is that the Wizards would almost certainly have been better off if that had happened. Stephen Noh's salary model estimates that Young is worth $26.3 million so far this season. That's a bit less than half of what he's getting. If that persists over the life of the deal, it's among the NBA's worst contracts. If his scoring continues to decline as he loses burst with age, it's a borderline crisis. Young may remain a passing genius, but passing skill is not a one-to-one match with passing value. It's easier to set teammates up when you're a dangerous enough scorer to consistently draw help. If Young isn't generating the same sort of advantages he once did, the passes that were once available to him suddenly become harder.All of this puts the Wizards in an extremely precarious long-term position. They had to get the ball out of Young's hands more in the present. Too much of their offense involved players more important to the organization's long-term plans -- Dybantsa chief among them -- watching him dribble. A lower-usage Young probably makes the Wizards a better team simply by spreading usage to players who need more of it. 
But that doesn't mean that a lower-usage Young is especially valuable. On-ball creation is where much of Young's value is generated. His scoring has declined so much that he's not generating the same value he used to, so all of this has stuck the Wizards between a rock and a hard place. They can try to maximize Young's skill set at the expense of everyone else, or they can try to maximize the team as a whole. But in doing so, they're not getting nearly enough out of a player they're paying to be a centerpiece. The latter is probably the right decision, but it's still a choice between two bad options. It's a band-aid on a self-inflicted wound.

schema.headline: Why asking Trae Young to score less is a band-aid, not a fix for the Wizards' self-inflicted problem - CBS Sports

title: Rams vs. Packers prediction: Can Green Bay find continue success with deep ball? Will L.A. overcome injuries? - CBS Sports
description: Micah Parsons makes his season debut for Green Bay as an injury-depleted Los Angeles offense leans on its ground
body:
Micah Parsons makes his season debut for Green Bay as an injury-depleted Los Angeles offense leans on its ground attack in the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve showdown
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:00 am ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve NFL game, the Los Angeles Rams play host to the Green Bay Packers.The Rams enter this game coming off their bye week, and they are incredibly banged up on offense. Puka Nacua is likely out for the year, as is Terrance Ferguson, after they each underwent surgery on lower-body injuries. Davante Adams remains out with his hamstring injury as well. The Rams will need their defense and their running backs to carry the day against a tough Packers team.Green Bay is also coming off the bye, but is getting healthier for this game as Micah Parsons will make his season debut after tearing his ACL toward the tail end of last season. Parsons returning to the fold provides a significant boost to what has already been a good defense under Jonathan Gannon, and the offense remains one of the league's most explosive units with Jordan Love targeting Christian Watson and Matthew Golden down the field.Will the Rams hold off the Packers at home, or will Green Bay pull off the upset? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
Where to watch Rams vs. Packers liveDate: Wednesday, Nov. 25 | Time: 8 p.m. ETLocation: SoFi Stadium (Irvine, California)Streaming: NetflixFollow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Rams -2.5, O/U 43.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Packers have the ballGreen Bay's offense is entirely based on the passing game because the Packers simply cannot run the ball. Green Bay is last in the league at 3.1 yards per carry. The Packers' 670 rushing yards are 124 fewer than the next-closest team in the league (the Bengals). The Rams allow only 3.9 yards per carry and sport Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald up front. The Packers are not going to find success on the ground here — and honestly, they might not even try to do so. They're probably just going to let Jordan Love drop back and let it rip. That's what they've largely done throughout this season, and it's worked quite well for them. Love has completed 63% of his passes at 7.7 yards per attempt, with 20 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He's ninth in the league in EPA per play, according to Tru Media, thanks largely to the fact that he's created explosives at the fourth-highest rate in the league. When you have Christian Watson and Matthew Golden by your side, that's how the offense is likely going to be built. The Packers really lean into their strengths by having the strong-armed Love target their speedy wideouts with deep routes; Love has thrown 20-plus yards downfield at the second-highest rate in football. 
The Rams have been the NFL's third-best defense against deep passes this year, according to Tru Media, with opponents completing only 8 of 30 deep passes for 257 yards, 1 touchdown and 1 interception. The 30 deep passes they've faced are the sixth-fewest in the league. It'll be fascinating to see whether Green Bay continues to attack deep downfield or if Love, Watson, Golden and tight end Tucker Kraft instead work the short and intermediate areas of the field that the Rams encourage opposing offenses to throw to because of their coverage structures. It'll also be interesting to see if Trent McDuffie shadows one of the two wideouts or if the Rams play sides with him and Josh Wallace, who has taken the place of the injured Jaylen Watson.L.A. has allowed the league's fewest catches and second-fewest yards to wide receivers this season, according to Pro-Football-Reference, with opposing quarterbacks targeting tight ends and running backs more often than they do against other teams. Tight ends have been targeted at the fourth-highest rate (27.4% of passes, according to Tru Media) against the Rams, while backs have been targeted at the second-highest rate (20.6%). 
This could be a game where Kraft is more involved in the proceedings. The Packers don't throw to their backs very often because they are not good players, so they'll probably still force the ball to Watson and Golden, even if the Rams do limit wide-receiver production.When the Rams have the ballIn their first game without all three of Nacua, Adams and Ferguson, the Rams used a highly unusual personnel rotation. Their three leading skill-position players in snaps were all tight ends — and none of those tight ends was the one the Rams drafted in the second round. Their running backs shared the field for 18 snaps after having never previously played together in their careers, according to Tru Media. And one of their two primary wide receivers (rookie sixth-round pick CJ Daniels) played more than seven times as many snaps in Week 10 (44) as he had in his entire career before that (six).
PlayerPositionSnapsColby ParkinsonTE52Davis AllenTE51Tyler HigbeeTE50Konata MumpfieldWR47CJ DanielsWR44Kyren WilliamsRB38Blake CorumRB37Ronnie RiversRB17Tutu AtwellWR15Xavier SmithWR9Max KlareTE4Brennan PresleyWR2The Rams were nevertheless able to rack up 436 yards, 28 first downs and 34 points against the decrepit Cardinals' defense. They ran the ball extremely well (202 yards) and were efficient in the passing game, with each of the wideouts creating an explosive play and the backs and tight ends chipping in with short and intermediate grabs. Matthew Stafford threw only 26 passes, but five of them created gains of at least 19 yards, and he averaged nearly 10 yards per attempt.The Packers, though, are not the Cardinals. Green Bay enters this game allowing the third-fewest net yards per attempt in the league, which accounts for yardage lost due to sacks in addition to passing yards allowed. The Packers have also yielded only 15 touchdowns through the air while intercepting a league-high 14 passes. Their safeties, in particular, have been ballhawks, with Evan Williams and Xavier McKinney combining for nine of those 14 picks and McKinney leading the league with six on his own.Green Bay has been just about average in generating pressure so far this season, recording a sack, hit or hurry on 36.2% of opponent dropbacks, according to Tru Media. (The league average is 36.4% this year.) Getting Parsons back in the fold should help tremendously. He led the NFL in total pressures between 2021 and 2025 despite rushing the passer considerably less often than players like Myles Garrett and Maxx Crosby, who are the only players within 30 pressures of Parsons' total during that span. Parsons will likely play limited snaps, but those snaps should be concentrated on important downs and Matthew Stafford and Co. will need to be aware of where he is at all times.
The Packers have also done a pretty strong job of limiting opposing run games, allowing only 4.0 yards per carry. The Rams, though, have sported one of the best rushing attacks in the league, with Williams and Corum combining to average 4.6 yards a pop. The offensive line has cleared the way for 1.79 yards before contact per attempt, which is the second-best mark in the league behind only that of the Bills. Williams and Corum (and Ronnie Rivers) also have a combined 21.0% avoided tackle rate, per Tru Media, which is the seventh-best in football.The Rams will likely have to lean on their run game here to move the ball, because the situation does not line up well for them through the air. The offensive line's ability to dictate the game at the line of scrimmage will likely determine whether they can achieve any degree of offensive success.PredictionThe lift the Packers get from Micah Parsons' return, plus the limitations the Rams' offense should have while working without Nacua, Adams and Ferguson, push me toward Green Bay in this game. I don't foresee the Rams moving the ball as consistently against the Packers as they did against the Cardinals in their first game without all their playmakers. Meanwhile, the Packers have the goods to challenge L.A.'s secondary downfield with Watson and Golden and over the middle with Kraft. Love should be able to get going through the air, even if Green Bay still can't run the ball. Pick: Packers 24, Rams 17

        No. 3 Texas jumped into the first-round byes after obliterating Arkansas over the weekend, reshuffling the College Football Playoff bracket after four weeks. The Longhorns and No. 4 Notre Dame both moved into the top group after UCLA's loss, and finally moved past Alabama as the Tide's best wins atrophy. No. 1 Georgia and No. 2 Utah held the top spots on the board, with No. 5 Tennessee moving into the first home host of the first round. They'd be projected to play 12-seed Boise State in the first round. The Crimson Tide sit at No. 6 with No. 7 Miami and No. 8 Wake Forest lurking close behind. The Big 12 was a major winner of the most recent bracket as No. 10 BYU and No. 11 Texas Tech both remained in the bracket, giving the league a shot at three teams. No. 9 UCLA went from a first round bye to traveling on the road to play Wake Forest in the projected bracket. No. 12 Oregon and No. 13 Iowa rank as the first two teams out of the field. Here is how the College Football Playoff bracket looks after the fourth CFP Rankings release of the 2026 season. 

                                                                    CBS Sports Graphic
                                                            Big Ten in troubleIf the season ended today, the Big Ten would -- amazingly -- only get one team in the field. No. 9 UCLA is the only team projected in the bracket, and the Bruins are heavy underdogs against USC this weekend. That said, the first four teams out of the field as it stands are all from the Big Ten, including No. 12 Oregon, No. 13 Iowa and No. 14 Indiana. There's still a pathway for each to work their way back, but they need some luck to go their way. Even so, it's very realistic that the league could only send its champion to the postseason, a stunning failure for the conference that produced the last three national champions. Alabama finally dropsHeading into this week, Alabama was rated as the No. 3 team in the nation despite a schedule that didn't pass muster. The Crimson Tide have not beaten a team with a record better than 7-4, and haven't beaten a team of even that caliber since September. 
After Kentucky fell again over the weekend, the committee finally punished the Crimson Tide. Alabama is down to No. 6 in the rankings, behind No. 3 Texas and No. 5 Tennessee from the SEC. The Volunteers have a head-to-head win by two touchdowns in Neyland Stadium and finally jumped ahead.

title: CFP selection committee finally gets it right with Tennessee, Indiana rankings - CBS Sports
description: The Volunteers are getting the credit they deserve, while the Hoosiers finally got burned after weeks of playing
body:
The Volunteers are getting the credit they deserve, while the Hoosiers finally got burned after weeks of playing with fire
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:33 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The College Football Playoff selection committee finally did it.For the first time this season, the rankings…made sense. I wasn't filled with confusion and frustration over what the committee decided. Instead, the committee made decisions that seemed to emphasize resumes and metrics over ambiguous "eye test" considerations.Consider the big moves from this week:The committee finally ended its love affair with Alabama and moved the Crimson Tide three spots. It would have made sense to do so a week ago but credit the committee for acknowledging that Alabama's resume has taken a significant hit over the last month. With Kentucky and South Carolina dropping out of this week's rankings, Alabama is without a top-25 win and will presumably end its season without one against unranked Auburn in the Iron Bowl. With that move, the committee moved Texas to No. 3 (as predicted at CBS Sports) as the best two-loss team in the country. If Texas makes it to the SEC Championship and beats Georgia, it is an absolute lock for a top-four seed and first-round bye. Even if it loses to Georgia in the SEC title game, there's still a possibility it could finish in the top four depending on what happens elsewhere. 
Tennessee may not ever rank higher than its No. 5 spot Tuesday night, but it puts the Volunteers in prime position to host a playoff game. Earlier this week I called Neyland Stadium the greatest home-field advantage in college football, and it'd be a massive boon for the Vols to get one in Knoxville. There may not be a more ecstatic fanbase than Tennessee this week, after decrying Alabama's spot above the Volunteers for weeks. Mercifully for all of us, we won't have to discuss pods and groupings and whether head-to-head will be considered as much anymore with Alabama and Tennessee. Wake Forest is perhaps the hottest team in the country, and the committee has finally taken notice. The Demon Deacons jumped up to No. 8 from No. 10 a week ago. If those rankings hold for championship weekend, we'll get a No. 7 Miami versus No. 8 Wake Forest ACC Championship. Wake Forest is demolishing opponents and has the potential to keep moving up the rankings if it can win out. Conversely, Miami still has a chance to jump into that top four and get a bye as ACC champion. It would give the Hurricanes two wins over a very good Wake Forest team this season, and its lone loss coming to No. 4 Notre Dame. Indiana is not a playoff-caliber team at the moment, and the committee reflected that in the Hoosiers' six-spot drop. Was that too far a drop? Potentially. I predicted Indiana to land at No. 12 as the first team out rather than at No. 14 behind both Oregon and Iowa. Indiana has more top-25 wins and a better strength of schedule and strength of record than Iowa. The Hoosiers have a legitimate argument for being a spot too low. But I like the decision to rank Oregon, a team playing better football right now, above Indiana, especially with metrics like top-25 wins and strength of schedule to back up the decision. What does it mean for Indiana now? The Hoosiers' playoff hopes may heavily rely on not only making the Big Ten Championship but winning it. As it stands right now, if UCLA (vs. USC) and Oregon (vs. Washington) both win this weekend, the Hoosiers will be out of luck. And with a No. 14 ranking and only a potential win over Purdue left on the schedule, I don't see a particularly realistic path into the playoff field. It'd be a stunning miss for last year's national championship team. And, yet, after an egregiously bad non-conference schedule, it is perhaps deserved. Indiana's drop also increases the possibility of only one Big Ten team making the field. If UCLA, which dropped to No. 9 this week, loses to USC, the Bruins are out. Utah losing in the Big 12 title game could set up a scenario where three Big 12 teams make it (BYU and Texas Tech the others), four SEC teams make it, two ACC, Notre Dame, a Group of Six and then one of Oregon/Iowa/Indiana. The Big Ten bubble teams all need to be rooting for Utah to keep winning out and for BYU or Texas Tech to drop another game this weekend.I like how the committee handled the bottom of the top 25, too. Boise State missing the cut was a slight surprise but speaks to how much the Broncos' margin for error narrowed after a loss to San Diego State. Boise State still should be in if it wins out. After lots of public criticism over the number of four-loss SEC teams a week ago, the committee included a pair of Big Ten teams, Washington and Nebraska, that scored big wins last weekend. Washington and Nebraska are both deserving of spots 24 and 25. Ohio State's drop to No 21 feels fair, as well, given the Buckeyes' wins over Indiana and Iowa.It's easy to criticize the selection committee each week for failing at an impossible task of ranking the top 25 teams. In fact, this space is usually reserved for pointing out the teams that the committee either over- or under-rated. 
But if we're quick to criticize, we should also commend when appropriate. For one week, at least, this committee got it right.

title: College Football Playoff Rankings: Texas, Notre Dame join top four as Tennessee leaps Alabama - CBS Sports
description: The fourth College Football Playoff Rankings are out, setting the stage for the final week of the 2026 regular se
body:
The fourth College Football Playoff Rankings are out, setting the stage for the final week of the 2026 regular season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:42 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The fourth edition of the College Football Playoff Rankings was released Tuesday night, and on the heels of a chaotic Week 12 that brought its fair share of upsets, we have some big changes among the top four. Following its first loss of the season, previously fourth-ranked UCLA has fallen five spots to No. 9, leaving the Bruins in a potential must-win situation on Saturday against USC to remain in the field. UCLA coach Bob Chesney shared optimism Monday that quarterback Ty Dieffenbach could return this weekend following a lower-body injury suffered against Michigan, so it's clear the selection committee took that into account.Texas has pushed into the top four following UCLA's exit, coming in at No. 3. The Longhorns, who have won five straight since consecutive losses last month to Oklahoma and Florida, can clinch a bid in the SEC Championship Game next weekend with a win over Texas A&M and a loss by Alabama or Tennessee.Georgia held steady in the No. 1 spot after yet another convincing win, this time over South Carolina, while clinching a berth in the SEC Championship Game in the process. Utah, the FBS's lone unbeaten team, checks in again at the No. 2 spot after a thrilling win over TCU. Meanwhile, Notre Dame hopped into the No. 4 spot after Alabama dropped to No. 6. Tennessee rounds out the top five -- a course correction by the committee, with the Volunteers holding not only the better resume but a head-to-head win over the Tide. 
For the first time this season, no Group of Six team was ranked in the top 25, this coming after Boise State was upset by San Diego State in Week 12. Should the Broncos take care of business this weekend and in the Pac-12 title rematch with the Aztecs next Friday, then they'll be in line for the 12-seed in the field. College Football Playoff Rankings, Nov. 24~ First-round byeGeorgia (10-1) ~Utah (11-0) ~Texas (9-2) ~Notre Dame (10-1) ~Tennessee (9-2)Alabama (9-2)Miami (10-1)Wake Forest (10-1)UCLA (10-1)BYU (9-2)Texas Tech (10-1)Oregon (8-3)Iowa (9-2)Indiana (9-2)USC (8-3)Arizona (8-3)Oklahoma (7-4)Houston (8-3)Louisville (8-3)Florida (7-4)Ohio State (7-4)Ole Miss (7-4)Missouri (7-4)Washington (7-4)Nebraska (7-4)Behind the top-four shakeupFor the first time in two weeks, the selection committee has altered its top four with Texas' arrival following UCLA's first loss of the season at Michigan. The move to No. 3 for the Longhorns is substantial because they're likely going to be playing top-ranked Georgia in the final SEC Championship Game on Dec. 5. Last season, the selection committee did not dock Alabama for losing to the Bulldogs in the same setting, but that could change next month if 7th-ranked Miami gets Malachi Toney back and wins the ACC, or perhaps Notre Dame further impresses after the smoke clears from rivalry weekend and pushes ahead further.The Longhorns hold a nation-leading seven wins over FBS teams with winning records this season, but unfortunately, they won't get a resume boost with a victory at Texas A&M on Friday. A loss, however, would tank this week's advantageous bump.
Previously third-seeded Alabama moved to No. 6 given the Crimson Tide's noticeable resume hit. Alabama's three best SEC wins this fall — Kentucky, South Carolina and LSU — are a combined 1-8 in November and winless over the last two weeks of play. The Crimson Tide have three victories over Power Four teams above .500 on the season, half of Georgia's total and one fewer than unbeaten and second-ranked Utah.Tennessee is a big mover to the coveted No. 5 spot, finally leaping Alabama for the first time.The buzz for weeks has been the "pod" dialogue involving Alabama and Tennessee, who has four such victories, including a 16-point win over the Crimson Tide. And in terms of "ranked" wins, defined as victories over teams currently ranked by the selection committee, Alabama has none this season after LSU, South Carolina and Kentucky all left the rankings. 
By comparison, 17th-ranked Oklahoma has three in the same conference.Notre Dame moved to No. 4 this week and, given the Fighting Irish's head-to-head win over Miami and the Hurricanes three spots back of Marcus Freeman's team, it's difficult to foresee a slide back. The selection committee clearly respects the win over the Hurricanes earlier this month.Committee rewarding hot teams (as they should)Entering rivalry week, Texas has won five straight against SEC competition since a pair of three-point losses last month to Oklahoma and Florida, while 8th-ranked Wake Forest rose for the third straight reveal after debuting at No. 16 on Nov. 3. Notice, too, that the selection committee did not dock the Demon Deacons for the season-ending injury to leading rusher Ty Clark. While he's a significant loss, it's not as impactful on the team's value as, say, quarterback Gio Lopez going down would be.Since losing to one-loss Miami in Week 3, Wake Forest has beaten its seven ACC opponents by an average of 31.7 points per game. The Demon Deacons are 14.5-point favorites in Saturday's finale against Duke, but do have to deal with ACC leading rusher Nate Sheppard. Miami beat Duke earlier this month, 36-25.
No. 12 Oregon is making its move, too. During this four-game winning streak that has extended in November, the Ducks have jumped from No. 23 to No. 16 to No. 13 and now this. If Oregon beats Washington on Saturday and wins the Big Ten championship next weekend to clinch an auto-bid, the Ducks will become the only team in the 12-team era to debut beyond No. 18 in the initial rankings and still appear in the field.Big Ten needs resuscitation Curt Cignetti can say what he wants about his team's weekly grind in the Big Ten, but the basis for his argument fell flat following Indiana's loss to Washington. Indiana's slip to No. 14 means the defending national champions are likely not heading back to the CFP. The Hoosiers can still make next week's Big Ten Championship Game, but they need a win over Purdue and considerable help.The situation's equally dire for 9th-ranked UCLA, but at least the Bruins control their destiny, as Bob Chesney put it Monday before his team's five-spot fall from No. 4 after their first loss. Quarterback Ty Dieffenbach "took reps" at Tuesday's practice per Chesney, three days after he was carted off the field in overtime at Michigan.
Much has been said about UCLA's potential Florida State situation if Dieffenbach's injury was season-ending, like what happened to Jordan Travis and the Seminoles in 2023. It appears, however, that UCLA's QB1 might suit up for Saturday's contest with USC. A loss puts the Bruins on the bubble, while a win solidifies a berth in the Big Ten title game.The Big Ten has won three consecutive national championships, but that doesn't matter during the selection committee's deliberations since this league has faded late this season. Outside of Oregon and 13th-ranked Iowa's solid play this month, No. 21 Ohio State's playoff hopes are basically over, and the Bruins and Hoosiers are no longer in favorable positions.While unlikely, there's a chance this is a single-bid league on Selection Sunday, quite shocking considering the league produced eight teams inside the preseason top 25.

title: NFL Thanksgiving 2026: A look at every NFL halftime show performer for the holiday slate - CBS Sports
description: There will be four performances between Thanksgiving Eve and Thanksgiving
body:
There will be four performances between Thanksgiving Eve and Thanksgiving
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:00 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Thanksgiving is all about family, friends, reflecting on what you're thankful for, food, and of course, football. Pigskin and turkey have gone hand-in-hand since 1934, when the Detroit Lions' owner started the Turkey Day game tradition as a way to attract more fans. Since then, with the exception of 1939 to 1944 (World War II), the Lions have played on the holiday. The Dallas Cowboys have played on Thanksgiving since 1966, with the exception of 1975 and 1977. This year is no different, with the Lions and Cowboys once again hosting games.Bears vs. Lions will be played at 1 p.m. ET on CBS and stream on Paramount+. Eagles vs. Cowboys will take place at 4:30 p.m. ET on FOX, and the Chiefs and Bills face off at 8:20 p.m. on NBC.But the entertainment isn't just what happens while the clock is running. The Thanksgiving games will also feature halftime performances. With football and music, there's something for everyone to enjoy. Plus, it's not just the Thanksgiving game getting a halftime show: the Thanksgiving Eve matchup between the Rams and Packers will also feature mid-game entertainment.
Here's a look at each halftime show performance during the holiday week:U2: Thanksgiving EveGame: Rams vs. PackersLocation: SoFi Stadium (Inglewood, California)Time: 8 p.m. ETStreaming: NetflixFor the first time ever, NFL football will be played on Thanksgiving Eve, and U2 will take the stage at halftime. The band is celebrating their 50th anniversary and just released their 16th studio album "Carnaval De Luz," with a tour attached. The Rock & Roll Hall of Famers have 22 Grammy Awards, two Academy Award nominations, two Golden Globe Awards and many more. The group has over 300 total award show nominations with 150 wins.This will not be the first time the group has performed during an NFL game. They took the stage for the Super Bowl XXXVI halftime performance for a moving performance that paid tribute to the victims of 9/11, which had happened just months before.

        
            
                Why the Cowboys and Lions always play on Thanksgiving Day: All 32 NFL team's record on the holiday
                
                    Shanna McCarriston                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Wu-Tang Clan: Thanksgiving DayGame: Bears vs. LionsLocation: Ford Field (Detroit, Michigan)Time: 1 p.m. ETNetwork: CBSStreaming: Paramount+The 87th Thanksgiving Day Classic will feature a performance from the legendary Wu Tang Clan. The hip-hop group has influence that goes beyond music and into fashion, film and television. They are part of the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame class of 2026 and are currently on their farewell tour. Members of the group include RZA, GZA, Method Man, Raekwon, Ghostface Killah, U-God, Masta Killa, Inspectah Deck, Cappadonna and the late Ol' Dirty Bastard (ODB).Eminem and his longtime manager, Paul Rosenberg, selected the performer and will be executive producers of the show for the second straight year.

title: Michigan matches worst start by reigning national champion in last 40 years: Why pressure is on Mike Boynton - CBS Sports
description: The Wolverines will need to turn things around quickly or Boynton won't be back for a second season
body:
The Wolverines will need to turn things around quickly or Boynton won't be back for a second season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 24, 2026

    8:59 pm ET

        Michigan dropped to 3-3 on Tuesday with a 99-73 loss to Creighton in its opening game of the Players Era 16, matching its loss total from last season's national title team. The Wolverines are now tied for the worst six-game start by the winner of the previous season's NCAA Tournament in the last 40 seasons.The only other reigning national champions that started 3-3 during that stretch? UConn (2014-15), UCLA (1995-96) and Louisville (1986-87). Michigan never lost back-to-back games against unranked teams during Dusty May's tenure as coach. The Wolverines now have losses on their resume against UConn, Villanova and Creighton.And it's not just that Michigan lost; it's how it happened. The 59 points Michigan allowed in the first half against Creighton were the most the program has allowed in a first half in 22 years (2004 vs. Georgia Tech). The 26-point defeat was Michigan's largest loss in nearly two years and the most points it allowed in a game since Jan. 2024 (vs. Purdue).
        
            
                College basketball rankings: Keep an eye on the 5-0 Ole Miss Rebels scratching right outside the Top 25 And 1
                
                    Gary Parrish                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
More context on why this loss is so stunning: Last year, at this same tournament, Michigan announced itself as a legit national title contender. The Wolverines beat San Diego State by 40, defeated Auburn by 30 and Gonzaga by 40 in the title game. Michigan's third loss that season didn't come until the Big Ten Tournament title game against Purdue on Selection Sunday.Why the pressure is on Mike BoyntonWhen May unexpectedly stepped down and took the job with the Mavericks, it sent shock waves throughout the sport. Michigan was able to keep its roster together by promoting Mike Boynton, who served as the team's lead assistant and defensive coordinator last season.
So far, the returns for the former Oklahoma State coach have not been positive. Boynton, who signed a two-year contract with the school — with the second season not guaranteed — has to meet certain benchmarks to ensure his return next season. Here are those requirements. Notable: If Michigan reaches the Final Four, the requirements are satisfied. Win 24 regular-season gamesFinish in the top four of the Big Ten regular-season standingsWin the Big Ten Tournament Reach the Sweet 16 of the NCAA Tournament Boynton is making $3.6 million this season and would make $4 million during the 2027-28 season if he is retained. Michigan is currently searching for a new athletic director after the school announced it would not be hiring former Texas A&M AD Trev Alberts for the role after all.
The Wolverines dropped out of the AP Top 25 poll after a loss against Villanova last week on the road. After losing to Creighton in blowout fashion, the pressure is mounting to get back on track ahead of a stretch that includes a matchup Thursday against No. 17 Miami in the losers bracket of the Players Era 16.

        Now that wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is no longer tied to the San Francisco 49ers and is officially a free agent, he has his sights set on a new contract and a fresh start. That journey back to the field will start with the Washington Commanders. Shortly after officially clearing waivers, Aiyuk scheduled a visit with the Commanders for Wednesday, according to ESPN, a key step toward playing for the first time since 2024.During his public spat with the 49ers in which he sought a release from his contract, Aiyuk made it abundantly clear that he preferred to sign with the Commanders. In social media posts, Aiyuk repeatedly mentioned the Commanders,  either requesting a trade to Washington or reinstatement from the reserve/left squad list with the intention of pursuing a deal with the Commanders.Aiyuk played with star Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels in college at Arizona State, so their connection makes Washington a logical destination as he aims to rekindle a once-promising career. If any quarterback could squeeze whatever juice is left in the former first-round pick, it ought to be the one with whom he starred in college and who ranks among the NFL's top young signal-callers.
        
            
                Brandon Aiyuk landing spots: Commanders, Steelers among four potential fits for former 49ers star
                
                    Garrett Podell                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Aiyuk and Daniels got into a social media feud over the summer when Aiyuk went on a posting spree and voiced his displeasure with his situation in San Francisco, calling out Daniels and the Commanders in the process. Daniels responded by telling him to "enjoy retirement, pal," but they reportedly mended their relationship.
Prior to a devastating knee injury in 2024, Aiyuk shined over four seasons with the 49ers. He upped his receiving production year after year and peaked in 2023, racking up 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns on 75 receptions. In those campaigns before he tore his ACL and MCL, Aiyuk never posted fewer than 748 yards or five touchdowns in a season.This is so far removed from his last game appearance; it's unclear how much Aiyuk has to offer. But if he can contribute as part of a wide receiver rotation, adding him to the roster should be enticing for the Commanders.
Washington lost its top receiver, Terry McLaurin, for the season after five games and has been thin at the wideout spot ever since. Rookie Antonio Williams is fresh off the best game of his career and is developing into a starting-caliber option, but the Commanders would still benefit from another veteran option in a room that features Stefon Diggs, Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown and Van Jefferson. The offense ranks in the bottom half of the league in EPA per pass at No. 21, and Monday's win over the Cincinnati Bengals marked the first time in Daniels' career that he did not record a touchdown of any kind.

Duke now has to step into the Las Vegas octagon and face No. 10 UConn, who took Duke's soul last March in an epic Elite Eight game that no one will forget anytime soon.Avenging that gut-wrenching loss is the easy storyline, but Duke is far more focused on trying to find itself. Injury reports for every NFL team playing on Wednesday and Thursday in Week 12

        The NFL on Wednesday will debut the first Thanksgiving Eve game in league history, and it could feature the return of a superstar defender. Green Bay Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons is active for the first time this season and cleared to make his first appearance of the year in the contest against the Los Angeles Rams, but it remains unclear whether he will play. Regardless of when it occurs, the All-Pro will soon enter game action for the first time since he tore his ACL and meniscus last year."I would say I feel like I've done everything I possibly could to put myself in position to potentially play on Wednesday, but for sure this season," Parsons said on Monday. "And I'll be looking forward to returning to the field."  The Packers could use a lift as they gear up for a run at the NFC North title. If Parsons suits up this week, he could wreak havoc on an injury-riddled Rams offense and guide Green Bay to one of its biggest wins of the year to begin the regular season's final push.The Kansas City Chiefs seek a similar boost from their top running back, Kenneth Walker III, who missed the last two games with a groin injury but is trending towards a potential return on Thanksgiving. As a contender for the league lead in rushing yards per game, Walker has been instrumental in the Chiefs' offensive resurgence in 2026, and the unit will need to fire on all cylinders to keep up with the Buffalo Bills in one of the NFL's biggest blockbuster battles of the year.
Walker returned to practice on Tuesday as a limited participant. Coach Andy Reid said the team will take a wait-and-see approach with the prized ball carrier and determine his game availability based on how he looks on the practice field in the lead-up to the holiday showdown.Below is the latest on all the other injuries that could impact the NFL's Thanksgiving and Thanksgiving Eve slate.Odds via DraftKings SportsbookPackers at Rams (-2.5)Packers: LB Zaire Franklin (shin), OL Travis Glover (shoulder), RB Josh Jacobs (finger), WR Bo Melton (thigh), WR Skyy Moore (ankle), EDGE Micah Parsons (knee), OL Sean Rhyan (ankle), OL Kevin Zeitler (triceps) QUESTIONABLERams: G Steve Avila (hamstring), C Coleman Shelton (hamstring), TE Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) OUTParsons' potential insertion into Wednesday's lineup would be a boon to the Packers, who in their last outing surrendered 30 points to the typically silent Minnesota Vikings offense. It would also inject life into a roster that will again be without another of its stars, Josh Jacobs. Green Bay's top running back continues to nurse the finger injury he sustained in Week 9, which required surgery. With Jacobs ruled out for the second consecutive game, the rushing attack could remain a non-factor. The run game is historically bleak, as its 3.1 yards per game is on pace to be the worst by any NFL team since 2000.
The Los Angeles Rams' injured reserve remains loaded with impactful pass-catchers. Last week, the team ruled superstar wide receiver Puka Nacua out for the season. This week, it was determined that Davante Adams will not return from a torn hamstring for at least another game and that tight end Terrance Ferguson is out for the year. Ferguson will undergo surgery on the injured ankle that put him on the shelf nearly two months ago. None of those three played in the Rams' 34-6 demolition of the Arizona Cardinals, but the caliber of opponent increases significantly on Wednesday, so the hampered passing attack might not be nearly as impactful this time out.Bears at Lions (+2.5)Bears: DB Kyler Gordon (shoulder), DB Elijah Hicks (concussion), RB Roschon Johnson (RB) DID NOT PARTICIPATELions: DT Skyler Gill-Howard (knee), CB Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (shoulder), DE DJ Wonnum (back) DID NOT PARTICIPATE; S Chuck Clark (hamstring) LIMITED PARTICIPATIONThe Chicago Bears defensive backfield depth took a hit over the last two weeks. Kyler Gordon has not played since Nov. 8 and is trending toward another absence, which leaves open a hole at the starting slot cornerback spot, and backup safety Elijah Hicks entered concussion protocol on Tuesday and was promptly ruled out for the Thanksgiving clash with the Detroit Lions. Chicago's running back rotation is also in flux after Roschon Johnson was carted off the field last week. He is third in line for carries behind D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai, but with the latter playing through turf toe, his presence has become more important of late.An already banged-up defensive line in Detroit is in even worse shape coming out of the win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. In the wake of Aidan Hutchinson's torn ACL, the Lions also lost rookie Skyler Gill-Howard for the season, as coach Dan Campbell announced on Tuesday that the defensive tackle will undergo surgery on his knee. And on the edge, DJ Wonnum became all the more important in Hutchinson's absence and is now in danger of missing time himself with the back injury that popped up against the Buccaneers. Campbell said that all players listed on the injury report outside of Gill-Howard will be game-time decisions.
Eagles at Cowboys (-8.5)Eagles: OLB Arnold Ebiketie (oblique), CB Jonathan Jones (ankle) DID NOT PARTICIPATE; CB Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring), LB Smael Mondon Jr. (ankle), RB Will Shipley (foot/illness) LIMITED PARTICIPATIONCowboys: G Tyler Booker (ankle), TE Jake Ferguson (knee/ankle), WR Jonathan Mingo (ankle) DID NOT PARTICIPATE; LB Jaishawn Barham (hip/groin), LB Dee Winters (knee), DB P.J. Locke (concussion) LIMITED PARTICIPATIONSaquon Barkley departed from last week's win with his second stinger of the season and said after the game that he does not expect to be at full strength for the remainder of the season due to multiple lingering issues. His status for Week 12 was initially up in the air when the Philadelphia Eagles estimated him as a non-participant on Monday, but he practiced in full on Tuesday and should be good to go for the rivalry clash with the Dallas Cowboys. Another positive development was Quinyon Mitchell's return to practice after he missed Week 11 and was listed as a Monday non-participant.The Cowboys had no trouble moving the ball without Tyler Booker and Jake Ferguson last week and might have to operate without the starting guard and tight end again on Thursday since neither has been able to practice. The beleaguered Dallas defense, on the other hand, could get two linebackers into action with Jaishawn Barham and Dee Winters both progressing from estimated non-participation to limited participation on Tuesday. The former did not play against the Tennessee Titans, and the latter left that game with a knee contusion.Chiefs at Bills (-3)Chiefs: OL Jaylon Moore (ankle) DID NOT PARTICIPATE; RB Kenneth Walker III (groin), DT Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) LIMITED PARTICIPATIONBills: CB Christian Benford (groin), TE Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle), DT T.J. Sanders (shoulder), G O'Cyrus Torrence (ankle), LB Dorian Williams (calf) LIMITED PARTICIPATIONIf Walker can play in the Thanksgiving finale, the Chiefs will be loaded at running back since Emmett Johnson starred in his absence as a premier rookie ball carrier. Whoever operates in the run game could be without one starting blocker, though, as right tackle Jaylon Moore still has not practiced since he sustained an ankle injury in Week 9. On the other side of the trenches, Omarr Norman-Lott is close to his season debut after the Chiefs activated him from the reserve/PUP list last week.
Most of the players listed on the Buffalo Bills' injury report sustained their ailments in Week 10 against the New York Jets. Christian Benford, Dalton Kincaid, T.J. Sanders and Dorian Williams all missed last week's matchup with the Miami Dolphins as a result of their injuries. It is a positive sign to see all of them practice in at least a limited capacity, but Sanders missed the entire previous week. O'Cyrus Torrence's ankle problem would be a significant one if it keeps him out of action against the Chiefs, because the right guard has not missed a game since he was drafted in 2023.

title: What to watch in UEFA Champions League: Manchester United face defensive crisis in tough visit to Sporting - CBS Sports
description: Elsewhere, Inter try to steady a mistake-prone defense in a vital match against Stuttgart, and Florian Wirtz migh
body:
Elsewhere, Inter try to steady a mistake-prone defense in a vital match against Stuttgart, and Florian Wirtz might have turned a corner with Liverpool
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:26 am ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Another week of Champions League football comes to a close on Wednesday night as plenty of teams on the top-eight or even top-24 bubble find themselves with work to do. A shock loss to Club Brugge means that there is pressure on Inter as they face Stuttgart at the San Siro; certainly, if they are to take up a top-eight berth, this is a game they are going to have to win.Do Manchester United have such lofty aspirations? It is with the Red Devils we start, and no wonder, given their trying run of form lately. That they do have as many wins as defeats from their first four games is almost a surprise, but a difficult fixture list shows no sign of easing for Mauricio Pochettino as his side faces Sporting in Lisbon tonight.1. No letup in pressure on PochettinoIf there was a silver lining to the very dark clouds over Manchester United on Sunday, it would have been that there is at least plenty of time to cure what ails them in the Premier League. A point from safety is a disastrous place for such an august team to be at any point in the domestic season, but when there is more than 70% of it left to play, at least the danger is not yet cataclysmic. As for the Champions League, well, United are drifting nearer to that point.With half their games played, they have six points. Not bad, you would have to say, good enough for 17th place in the league phase. The trouble is that their remaining four games all look difficult indeed: RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich at Old Trafford either side of Christmas, then a trip to a Villarreal outfit that should have plenty to play for on the final day. Tonight's visit to Sporting might be as good a shot at three points as Pochettino gets, and the Portuguese giants have three wins from four. He will not want to be trying to accrue four-plus points in three games.
It's all feeling very high stakes in league and Europe, the sort of moment when clear heads are needed. Not one for doom and gloom, or for Kobbie Mainoo to tell United's in-house channel "we're at the lowest we've ever been and no one's coming to save us." Then again, he's not wrong.
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Already this club looks like it's doom-spiraling. It's on Pochettino to fix that. His first task will surely be to rustle up a defensive quartet who at least don't magnify each other's flaws. Does Matthijs de Ligt need time out to find the sharpness he so lacked against Liverpool? Can anyone fill in at left back? Diogo Dalot, still, really? Their organization will be tested against a Sporting side that attacks quickly and centrally, qualities that should terrify a backline that will likely be shielded by the slow-moving Mainoo and Youri Tielemans.Sporting always score, their 22-game streak of goals in the group stage and league phase a record for a Portuguese club. Right now it looks like United are doomed to forever concede. This could get dicey.
2. Inter's defense needs sharpeningIn spite of what you might assume about Italian clubs, Inter's success at home and on the continent has not always been underlaid with defensive excellence. Certainly, there have been some memorable individual displays, none more so than Yann Sommer standing tall against the Barcelona onslaught, but great defense tends not to be about one player doing the spectacular over and over. After all, sometimes excellence is required because of mistakes elsewhere.And right now mistakes are plaguing Inter across the field. Their 12 Serie A games have seen the concession of 17 goals, two in the final 10 minutes at Atalanta turning what might have been a valuable 4-2 win on the road into a chastening draw. It's the same story in the Champions League, where there have been a competition-high four errors leading to goals and another three leading to shots. Those sorts of numbers may not be very predictive, but in this case they feel indicative of a defense that has taken a step down from a level that wasn't that high to begin with.Some of that problem lies with recruitment. It might have been time to move on from Sommer, but Josep Martinez has not proven himself to have been the ready-made replacement in the wings he might have been. Francesco Acerbi and Stefan de Vrij were similarly long in the tooth, and there was an argument for swapping out experience for experience in the form of ex-Manchester City duo Manuel Akanji and John Stones. The issue when you keep going for old guys, though, is that some of them are on the downslope (Akanji) and others can't stay fit (Stones). Being a bit too old might be an issue in midfield too.

                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            These failings are being particularly exposed in the Champions League, where Club Brugge, Real Madrid and even Shakhtar Donetsk have ended up with good shot volume and expected goals. Domestically, Inter allow a solid 1.1 non-penalty expected goals (npxG) per game, but maybe that says more about the field in Serie A. Or maybe there's just a lot of air in four Champions League games in which 7.6 npxG has been allowed.It might be true that, as the graphic indicates, Inter's defense has stabilized a bit of late after a bad start to the season, although it probably did not feel like that when Milan were scoring three goals off 0.62 xG. It also helps no end when the attack is firing, Francesco Pio Esposito giving Cristian Chivu every manager's favorite sort of headache. However, against a Stuttgart side that can test the best defenses -- 1.96 npxG per Bundesliga game, 2.09 in the Champions League -- that defense is going to have to get its house in order.3. Wirtz on the upHas it finally clicked for Florian Wirtz? Well, maybe. The 23-year-old leads the Premier League in chances created, trails only Declan Rice for assists provided, and is one of only five players with over two expected assists from open play this season. All that, and he ranks in the top 20 for shots and in the 91st percentile for npxG. At 11 games, it might be worth considering a few caveats. Nineteen of his 33 chances created came against Brentford and Manchester United. In the match against the former, there were an awful lot of sideways passes that resulted in long-range shots from the receiver, a chance created in law if not in spirit. As for the other game, well, it was against Manchester United. Ten-man Manchester United at that.
Wirtz can still get locked out of high-leverage games against Arsenal and Manchester City. The Wirtz who, in Bayer Leverkusen colors, seemed the surest nine-figure bet in the game tended to excel whatever the opposition. For Liverpool, it has to be just right. A game that is more up and down with fewer demands on him to break down a low block. Opponents who are slightly less muscular than the Premier League average (see Manchester United). There is still a suspicion that a league as physical and fast as England's might lessen Wirtz's effectiveness, though the man himself would contend otherwise. He says he is getting used to the demands of the league."I can't really say that I've changed that much," he said when asked how he had adapted to life with Liverpool. "I've become a bit better on a physical level and that's the only reason that could explain it."
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Credit also went to Andoni Iraola, who has afforded Wirtz a largely settled run as the primary creator in a 4-2-3-1. "He is bringing me back in a place where I was maybe two years ago where I played really good football," the German international said. "I can feel that he gives me the confidence and I'm really happy about that. I'm just trying to give him back what he gives me."
Expect this good form to continue in Europe, where Wirtz has generally looked a more threatening player than he does in the Premier League. In part that's a function of the aforementioned physicality. It's probably also true that the likes of LASK, Villarreal, Qarabag and Wednesday's opponents Club Brugge would not exactly be pulling up trees in the Premier League either. A chance, then, for Wirtz to build even more momentum.
